title: Avoid Duplicate Serialization in RSC Props
## Avoid Duplicate Serialization in RSC Props
The React Server/Client boundary serializes all object properties into strings and embeds them in th
- `async-defer-await` - Move await into branches where actually used
- `async-api-routes` - Start promises early, await late in API routes
- `bundle-conditional` - Load modules only when feature is activated
- `bundle-preload` - Preload on hover/focus for perceived speed
- `server-cache-lru` - Use LRU cache for cross-request caching
- `server-serialization` - Minimize data passed to client components
- `client-swr-dedup` - Use SWR for automatic request deduplication
- `rerender-defer-reads` - Don't subscribe to state only used in callbacks
- `rerender-memo` - Extract expensive work into memoized components
- `rerender-derived-state` - Subscribe to derived booleans, not raw values
- `rerender-functional-setstate` - Use functional setState for stable callbacks
- `rerender-lazy-state-init` - Pass function to useState for expensive values
- `rendering-animate-svg-wrapper` - Animate div wrapper, not SVG element
- `rendering-hydration-no-flicker` - Use inline script for client-only data
- `js-batch-dom-css` - Group CSS changes via classes or cssText
- `js-cache-function-results` - Cache function results in module-level Map
- `js-combine-iterations` - Combine multiple filter/map into one loop
- `js-length-check-first` - Check array length before expensive comparison
- `js-min-max-loop` - Use loop for min/max instead of sort

content.value_statement: React and Next.js applications often lose performance through waterfalls, large bundles, and avoidable re-renders. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code concrete review rules for faster frontend work.
actual_capabilities: Identifies sequential awaits that can be parallelized or moved closer to use.
Recommends bundle reductions through direct imports, dynamic imports, and deferred third-party loading.
Guides Server Component data fetching, serialization, caching, and server action authentication.
Reviews client-side data fetching patterns, global listeners, and storage access costs.
Suggests re-render and rendering improvements for memoization, effects, SVGs, and long lists.
Provides JavaScript micro-optimization guidance for repeated lookups, loops, sorting, and regular expressions.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not automated profiling or benchmark measurements.
It does not replace application-specific performance testing in production-like environments.
Some recommendations depend on the project framework version and build configuration.
It does not inspect live traffic, logs, databases, or deployed infrastructure.

use_cases.title: Review a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Check a React or Next.js change for waterfalls, oversized imports, server boundary issues, and unnecessary renders.

use_cases.title: Plan a Performance Refactor
use_cases.description: Turn vague performance concerns into focused tasks for data fetching, bundle size, and rendering behavior.

use_cases.title: Generate Better Components
use_cases.description: Ask an AI coding agent to produce React components that follow safer defaults for effects, state, and loading behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Component Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small React component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this React component using the Vercel React best practices skill. Focus on avoidable re-renders, effect dependencies, and simple rendering issues.

prompt_templates.title: Next.js Data Fetching Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of a Next.js page or route.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Next.js code for data fetching waterfalls, Suspense boundary placement, Server Component serialization, and cache opportunities.

prompt_templates.title: Bundle Size Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before shipping a large frontend feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this feature for bundle size risks. Check barrel imports, heavy initial components, third-party libraries, dynamic imports, and preload opportunities.

prompt_templates.title: End-to-End Refactor Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced performance planning across several files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a prioritized React and Next.js performance refactor plan. Include expected impact, files to change, test strategy, and tradeoffs for each recommendation.

output_examples.input: Review a page that awaits user data, configuration, and posts sequentially before rendering.
output_examples.output: The skill would flag the waterfall, suggest starting independent promises earlier, and recommend a Suspense boundary when only one section needs slower data.

output_examples.input: Review a component that imports several icons and a large editor on the initial route.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend direct package imports or optimized package imports, then move the editor behind a dynamic import with intent-based preloading.

output_examples.input: Review a Server Component that passes a complete user object to a small client component.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend passing only the fields used by the client component to reduce serialized payload size.

best_practices: Start with waterfalls and bundle size because they usually have the highest user-visible impact.
Keep recommendations tied to the specific code path, framework version, and user experience tradeoff.
Verify meaningful changes with tests, profiling, or bundle analysis when the project supports it.
anti_patterns: Do not apply memoization everywhere without proving that render work or reference instability matters.
Do not move data fetching to the client when Server Components can stream or serialize less data.
Do not lazy-load critical above-the-fold content when it would harm first paint or layout stability.

faq.question: Does this skill only apply to Vercel projects?
faq.answer: No. The guidance targets React and Next.js applications, including projects deployed outside Vercel.

faq.question: Can it automatically measure performance?
faq.answer: No. It provides review guidance and refactor patterns. You still need profiling, tests, or bundle analysis for measurement.

faq.question: Does it support React Server Components?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for Server Component data fetching, serialization, caching, and client boundary design.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it during edits?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is written for AI coding agents that write, review, or refactor React and Next.js code.

faq.question: Will every recommendation improve every app?
faq.answer: No. The skill describes tradeoffs, and some patterns depend on page priority, framework support, and runtime behavior.

faq.question: Is this a security skill?
faq.answer: No. It is mainly a performance and code quality skill, although it includes server action authentication guidance.
